text:
Closest findings support attribute-level discrimination and selective hard negatives, but no exact match surfaced combining GRU4Rec, a text encoder trained from scratch, and title/description-sensitive negatives. [MARS (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.00702) learns multiple attribute-aware text representations and matches user/item attributes, motivating finer distinctions than one pooled semantic vector; its pretrained-language-model setting does not establish effectiveness without pretrained weights. [UniT (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13530) identifies excessive clustering in text-based recommendation and uses general, sequence-driven, and popularity-driven pair sampling to selectively separate item representations. [DANSeR (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3744348) mines hard negatives sharing learned quantization codes with positives, providing an interaction-learned analogue of attribute-sensitive sampling; its backbone is graph-based rather than GRU.

A constraint-compatible research hypothesis: randomly initialized token embeddings plus a lightweight CNN or attention-pooling encoder over titles/descriptions; jointly fuse text and item-ID features before GRU4Rec, using the same learned item representation for candidate scoring. Train everything through next-item prediction within one network per category. Mix uniform negatives with a modest fraction sharing informative title tokens or nearby learned representations, excluding known training positives. These are proposed adaptations, not demonstrated results from the cited papers; text similarity alone cannot establish that a candidate is truly negative. [Context-Aware Negative Sampling (2025)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/11021640) reports improved diversity with a small accuracy loss, so harder sampling should be tested against the fixed macro validation HR@10 rather than assumed beneficial. Ablate text fusion first, then hard-negative sampling, preserving one jointly trained checkpoint per category.
